questions.answerText: Egg of T.solium is acid fast
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Egg of T.solium is acid fast

 

Taenia solium is a parasitic tapeworm that is primarily found in humans and pigs. It is a zoonotic parasite, (transmitted between animals and humans, often via consumption of contaminated food or water).

 

causes two distinct diseases:

 

Taeniasis – The adult tapeworm infection in the intestines of humans.

 

Cysticercosis – The larval form of the tapeworm (known as cysticerci) infecting tissues, particularly the brain, muscles, and eyes.


Life Cycle:
•    Definitive host: Humans, where the adult tapeworm lives in the small intestine.
•    Intermediate host: Pigs, where the larvae form cysts in the muscles and tissues.
 

Humans can also act as the intermediate host in case of autoinfection (via ingestion of eggs) leading to neurocysticercosis (NCC).
•    The egg of tenia solim is not acid fast- rather the eggof tenia saginata is acid fast.

 

Other options:

 

Option A. Egg of T.solium causes neurocysticercosis (NCC): True. If a person ingests T. solium eggs (from contaminated food, water, or feces), it can lead to neurocysticercosis.

 

Option C. albendazole is the DOC of NCC: True. albendazole is the drug of choice for treating neurocysticercosis. Albendazole alone or in combination with Praziquental can be given to treat case of NCC.

 

Option D. NCC is the most common cause of seizures in India: True. Neurocysticercosis is one of the most common causes of seizures in India, particularly in areas with poor sanitation and where pork consumption is prevalent.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Taenia solium eggs are not acid-fast, distinguishing them from Taenia saginata eggs which are acid-fast positive.

questions.stem: Man is both intermediate and definitive host for:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. T. solium

 

Taenia solium is a tapeworm that has a complex life cycle involving both intermediate and definitive hosts.

  • Definitive host: Humans (adults live in the human intestine).
  • Intermediate host: Humans (in case of cysticercosis — when humans ingest eggs or larvae from contaminated food/water, the larvae can develop into cysts in various tissues like muscles, brain, eyes, etc.).
     

 

Other Options:

 

Option B. T. saginata: Humans are the definitive host for T. saginata (beef tapeworm), but the intermediate host is cattle, not humans.
 

Option C. D. latum: Humans are the definitive host for Diphyllobothrium latum (fish tapeworm), and the intermediate host is fish, not humans.

 

Option D. Dicroftis hominis: This is a liver fluke affecting cattle and sheep, with an ant as the intermediate host. Humans are not involved in its life cycle.
 

Educational Objective: 

 

Taenia solium uniquely uses humans as both definitive host (intestinal tapeworm) and intermediate host (cysticercosis when larvae form tissue cysts).

questions.answerText: Both adult and larval stage are seen in humans
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Both adult and larval stage are seen in humans

 

The ovum of Hymenolepis nana (H. nana) is shown, causing Hymenolepiasis, caused by the dwarf tapeworm.
 

Smallest human tapeworm (~2–4 cm)
 

Unique feature: Humans are both definitive and intermediate host hence all the stages are seen in the humans itself 
 

No intermediate host is necessary
 

Transmission: Fecal-oral route — ingestion of embryonated eggs
 

Common in children, especially in crowded settings with poor hygiene


 

Other options:

 

Option A. Transmission is through ingestion of infected pork: this is incorrect, That refers to Taenia solium, not H. nana. H. nana is transmitted via ingestion of eggs (autoinfection or contaminated food/water).

 

Option C.The helminth causes a transient self-resolving infection in humans: this is incorrect While mild cases may be self-limiting, autoinfection can cause chronic and persistent infections, especially in children.
    

Option D. Drug of choice for this condition is albendazole: This is Incorrect – The drug of choice for Hymenolepis nana is praziquantel. Albendazole is not effective for H. nana.

 

Educational Objective: 

 

Hymenolepis nana uniquely completes its entire life cycle within humans, with both adult and larval stages present, eliminating the need for an intermediate host.

questions.stemHtml: Identify the organism from its egg in the picture?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Necator americanus

 

The eggs  shown in the picture are oval, thin-shelled, and contain a cleavage-stage embryo (typically 4–8 cell stage) when passed in stool.
 

Transmission: Filariform larvae in soil penetrate intact skin, usually through bare feet.
 

Other options: 

 

Option A: Enterobius vermicularis: shows eggs that are asymmetrical, oval, flat on one side (planoconvex) , non-bile stained

 

Option B. Trichuris trichiura: eggs are Barrel-shaped with bipolar plugs
 

Option C. Ascaris lumbricoides: it can excrete both fertilized and unfertilized egg in stool The fertilized egg is Round with Thick, triple-layered shell showing ovum in the centre while unfertilized eggs are Elongated, narrow, more irregular with shell thinner than the fertilized egg. Both the eggs are non-bile stained.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Hookworm (Necator americanus) eggs are oval, thin-shelled, and contain a 4-8 cell embryo when passed in stool. This segmented embryo is the key distinguishing feature from other helminth eggs: pinworm eggs are D-shaped, whipworm has barrel-shaped eggs with bipolar plugs, and roundworm eggs have thick triple-layered shells.

questions.stemHtml: This is a schematic diagram depicting body structure of which of these helminthes?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Wuchereria bancrofti

 

The peripheral smear in the question shows a microfilaria that is sheathed and stains clearly, the nuclei within the worm is discrete and do not extend to the tip of the tail suggesting an infection with Wuchereria bancrofti.  

 

Other options:

 

Option A. Loa loa: It is sheathed; nuclei extend to tail tip; diurnal periodicity

 

Option C. Brugia malayi: Sheathed; 2 terminal nuclei at tail tip (not continuous); smaller (~220 µm)

 

Option D. Onchocera volvulus: Unsheathed; found in skin snips, not blood.

 

Educational Objective:

 

To identify Wuchereria bancrofti microfilariae: look for sheathed microfilariae with discrete nuclei that DO NOT extend to the tail tip (leaves empty space at tail). Key differentiators: Loa loa has nuclei extending to tail tip, Brugia malayi has 2 terminal nuclei at tail, and Onchocerca is unsheathed and found in skin (not blood).
